focus_areas: Legibility and structure of text on book/CD spines
Geometric orthogonality of shelves and vertical supports
Realism of the white electronic device
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text on the book spines. In real photos, even blurry text retains linear structure. In AI images, it often becomes wavy or melts. Also, inspect the bottom-left corner for structural plausibility—does the shelf actually rest on a solid base? Check if the white device has any functional details (lens, buttons) or if it's just a smooth blob.
image_description: A close-up, slightly low-angle shot of a light-colored wooden bookcase filled with books and media cases. The bookcase features multiple horizontal shelves. The left section contains rows of what appear to be CD or DVD cases with colorful spines. The right section holds hardcover and paperback books, some stacked horizontally. A small white electronic device (possibly a baby monitor or camera) sits on one of the right-hand shelves. The wood grain is visible, and the lighting appears natural, casting soft shadows.

expert_testimonies.reason: To verify the orthogonality of the shelves and sides, checking for warping or non-Euclidean geometry in the wooden structure.
To confirm the primary object classification and distinguish it from similar furniture like shelving units or cabinets.
To check if individual items on the shelves have distinct boundaries or if they merge into each other (fusion artifacts).
To assess the realism of textures, specifically wood grain and the legibility of text on spines.

evidence.thinking_trajectory: The image appears to be clear and well-lit, showing a wooden bookshelf filled with books and DVDs. There are no visible signs of noise, compression, blur, or darkening.
